verified_apis.input: Local control bytes are decoded by the adapter with a strict UTF-8 TextDecoder; JSON.parse itself accepts only a string, never bytes.
verified_apis.observable_result: object root with 7 keys, 5 objects, 3 arrays, 5 strings including an escaped \u00e9 and quotes, 5 numbers, 2 booleans, 1 null, container depth 4
verified_apis.family_note: JSON.parse is an ECMAScript builtin implemented natively in V8 14.6.202.34-node.34 inside the node binary. A V8 coverage probe of the adapter on the pinned binary listed 84 scripts and no JSON parser script. Parser source lines are measured on Node.js 26.10.0 built from the official source tarball with Clang 20.1.8, with only deps/v8/src/json/json-parser.cc instrumented: 0 lines for node -e 0 and for the adapter's decode step without JSON.parse, 865 json-parser.cc/.h lines for the nested-object control (identical per-line counts on repeat), and 756 for the nested-array control. On the pinned official binary, the Docker project records gdb function-entry hits on v8::internal::JsonParser<...> symbols (21 of 142 for the nested-object control, 0 for a node -e 0 baseline, identical on repeat, 23 for the nested-array control), and a staged AFL++ proxy maps those function entries into tuples. Wrapper packages that call JSON.parse (parse-json, json-parse-even-better-errors, secure-json-parse, @hapi/bourne, fast-json-parse, @discoveryjs/json-ext) share this family.

unverified_documented_apis.reason: Fetch spec defines it as UTF-8 decode then the JSON.parse algorithm; same V8 family, not separately run.
Module loader path over the same JSON.parse family; not a local byte API and not run.

limit: One valid nested RFC 8259 object control (plus the fixed nested-array second control) verifies JSON.parse after strict UTF-8 decoding on Node.js 26.10.0, not every JSON variant, number range, reviver use, or BOM handling. V8 parser source lines come from a source-built Node.js of the same release, not the pinned official binary. They are replay counts; no V8 basic-block edge feedback reaches AFL++. The staged AFL++ bridge hashes gdb-observed function-entry sets into tuples; it misses inlined code and says nothing about lines, blocks, or edges.
